milestone.title: raul path graph rendering + blocked lane + execution-lane filter (fixes M102/M103 swimlane half-shipped surface)

intent.outcome: After this ships: (1) a `blocked` lane appears in `raul path` showing items that are `execution_status=blocked` (currently 5 milestones: M119-M123), sorted by their `depends_on` chain so the execution-order hint is visible; (2) the execution lane filters out blocked items (currently M119 and M124 leak into the execution lane head because the filter only checks `effective_lifecycle()`); (3) `raul path` renders as a swimlane graph — each lane is a row, each milestone is a box, `depends_on` connects boxes via arrows — not the current comfy-table output; (4) the review lane's Detail column surfaces finding counts (`open_self_findings=N · open_external_findings=M`) when N+M > 0. The fix closes the M102/M103 swimlane half-shipped surface (M103 AC-08 said 'swimlane rendering' but what shipped is a table) and adds the missing `blocked` lane that the M118-archive work exposed. (M125 includes a small fix to the finding-count helpers: empty-phase findings are now counted as self-phase review work, matching the M101 design intent that the CLI never exposed a `--phase` flag; M101 has 7 open empty-phase findings, all of which are now visible in the review lane's Detail column. The fix is 2 lines in `has_open_self_findings` and 4 lines in `open_findings_by_phase` with 4 lines of new test coverage.)

problem.description: Four UX gaps in `raul path` surfaced during the M119-M124 read pass: (1) the `blocked` lane is missing — blocked milestones (M119, M120, M121, M122, M123) all show up in the `execution` lane because `execution_lane` (`crates/mp/src/path_engine.rs`) only filters on `lifecycle in [approved, in-progress]` and doesn't see the `execution_status=blocked` flag. A casual reader sees M110/M119/M124 in the execution lane head and assumes M119 is next; it's actually waiting for you. (2) M103 AC-08 promised 'swimlane rendering of mp path lanes' but the current code is a comfy-table — no graph, no boxes, no connections. (3) The review lane shows M95/M100/M101/M102/M103 with `phase=needs-self-check`; the lane title is 'review' but the items are `lifecycle=done` and the data shape doesn't surface `open_self_findings` / `open_external_findings` even though those are computed. The user is in review mode and wants to know 'how many findings are open per milestone' before clicking. (4) Color discipline: blocked items should be red so they're visible at a glance; right now they share the green execution-lane color. Each of these is a small change in isolation; together they make the path actually navigable.

in_scope: Add a `blocked` lane to `mp path` and `raul path`. New lane filters `execution_status=blocked` (current code only sees lifecycle; this adds the status check). Sorts by `depends_on` chain (topological + parent-comes-first) so the user sees the execution-order hint.
Filter `execution_status=blocked` out of the `execution` lane. Currently M119 and M124 leak into the execution head; the fix adds the status check alongside the existing lifecycle check.

Render `raul path --all` and `raul path --lane <name>` as a swimlane graph. Each lane is a row; each milestone is a box with `M{ID} | title` content; `depends_on` arrows connect boxes within a row (for visual clarity). Box-drawing characters (┌─┐│└─┤├─ etc.) for the terminal. Boxes that share a `depends_on` chain are vertically aligned per row. The graph preserves the existing JSON shape — `crates/mp/src/path_engine.rs` builds `lane['items']` and `lane['dependencies']`; the renderer consumes the same JSON. The graph renderer is its own module (`crates/raul/src/render/path_graph.rs` or similar) so the table path can be removed or kept as a `--table` flag.

Show `open_self_findings=N · open_external_findings=M` in the review lane's Detail column when N+M > 0. The data is already computed in `path_engine.rs::review_lane` (`m.has_open_self_findings()`, `m.has_open_external_findings()`); the change is in the renderer's detail-string builder.

Color the blocked-status milestones in the (new) `blocked` lane in Red. The execution lane keeps its Green (only ready-to-execute items appear there now). The grooming lane stays Blue; the backlog lane stays Magenta. A small extension to `lane_color(name) -> Color` to handle the new lane name.

Test surface: `crates/raul/tests/path_lanes_v2.rs` (or extend the existing `path_lanes.rs`). Tests: (a) blocked items appear in the new lane, not execution; (b) execution lane head contains only unblocked items; (c) review lane Detail column includes finding counts when present; (d) the new lane is sorted topologically. Plus a snapshot test for the graph renderer (lane graph at a known fixture), since the table path is being replaced.

Documentation: update `docs/concepts/02 - Getting Started/INSTALL.md` (or wherever the path surface is documented) with the new `blocked` lane + the graph rendering. Cross-link from M102/M103 specs to this milestone as the 'swimlane half-shipped' follow-up.
out_of_scope: New graph types (e.g. box-and-line, sunburst, etc.) — this milestone picks one render (box-drawing) and ships it; future work can add others.
Refactoring `crates/mp/src/path_engine.rs` beyond the lane additions — the current shape is fine; we just add one more lane and one more filter.
TUI changes to `crates/raul/src/tui/` — out of scope; this is the CLI surface only.
`raul explain` and `raul status` rendering improvements — different surface; separate milestone if needed.
Performance: the current `mp path` builds all lanes on every call. M125 doesn't optimize; the canonical caching strategy is the M100 AC-04 path that M110 already shipped.

design_decisions.area: Why a `blocked` lane is a separate lane, not a sub-row in the execution lane:
design_decisions.choice: A separate lane. The execution lane's purpose is 'what's next to execute' (sorted by priority + dep DAG); the blocked lane's purpose is 'what's waiting' (sorted by dep chain so the user sees the order in which to unblock). Conflating them in one lane makes the execution head noisy (M110 + 5 blocked items, indistinguishable) and hides the wait-list. A separate lane is the same pattern as the existing `review` lane (review = items in the review pipeline, not on the active path).
design_decisions.rationale: Each lane has a single responsibility. The execution lane shows ready items; the blocked lane shows waits; the review lane shows review-pipeline items. The user can scroll through the 4 lanes independently.

design_decisions.area: Why the swimlane graph is the new default, with the table as a `--table` flag (not the other way around):
design_decisions.choice: Graph is the default; the existing table path is preserved under `--table`. M103 AC-08 named 'swimlane rendering' as the deliverable; the current code is a comfy-table that doesn't match. The graph is the spec-compliant surface. The table is a fallback for narrow terminals (so boxes don't wrap badly) and an opt-in for users who prefer the old look.
design_decisions.rationale: Spec compliance (M103 promised swimlane) + UX (a graph conveys dependency relationships the table can't) + backward compat (the table path stays available under a flag).

design_decisions.area: Sort the `blocked` lane by `depends_on` chain, not by `priority + id`:
design_decisions.choice: Topological (parent-first) sort. M119 (no deps) → M120 (deps: M119) → M121+M122 (deps: M119, M120, both) → M123 (deps: all four). This shows the user the order in which to unblock (start with M119; M120 is unblocked next; then M121/M122; then M123). Priority sort would be misleading — a low-priority item with a high-priority dep is still unblocked first.
design_decisions.rationale: Topological order matches how the user thinks about the unblock sequence. Priority sort is for the execution lane (ready items, where priority is the deciding factor).

design_decisions.area: Why the swimlane graph is a new module in `crates/raul/src/render/path_graph.rs` rather than extending the existing `path` command:
design_decisions.choice: A new renderer module. The `path` command is the data-shape layer (calls `mp` and emits JSON); the renderer is the visual layer. Separating them keeps the data shape stable for tests and for non-CLI consumers (e.g. a future TUI view of the same data). The table renderer and the graph renderer both consume the same path-engine JSON; either can be selected at the command layer via the `--table` flag.
design_decisions.rationale: Separation of concerns. The data layer (what's on the path) and the view layer (how it's shown) are independent. M102/M103 shipped the data; M125 ships the view.

design_decisions.area: Why empty-phase findings are treated as self (not as 'all' or as 'untyped'):
design_decisions.choice: Empty-phase findings are the default 'self' review work. Rationale: the M101 design intent is that findings drive the review lifecycle, and 'self' is the natural default (the executor's own self-check); 'external' is the explicit alternative (the coordinator's external review). M101's ER-3 surfaced that the CLI never exposed a `--phase` flag, so most real-world findings are filed with `phase: ''`. Treating empty as self is the natural default; treating empty as 'all' (the prior `open_findings_by_phase('')` semantic) would be ambiguous when the caller passes an explicit phase like 'external'. The semantic is consistent: phase is metadata; the default is self.
design_decisions.rationale: Self is the natural default. The fix is 2 lines in `has_open_self_findings` and a 3-arm match in `open_findings_by_phase`. The default-behavior question is settled by the M101 design intent (findings drive the review lifecycle; 'self' is the natural mode for an executor's self-check).

findings.description: AC-04 spec drift: path_graph::render uses tree characters (`├──` `└──`), not the spec'd box-drawing characters (`┌─┐│└─┤├─`) with arrows-connecting-boxes-in-a-row. The M125 spec text says: 'Each lane is a row; each milestone is a box; depends_on arrows connect boxes within a row. Box-drawing characters (┌─┐│└─┤├─).' The implementation in crates/raul/src/path_graph.rs::render_dag_lane produces an ASCII tree, not a row-of-boxes.
findings.author: code-review-agent
findings.rationale: Spec wording explicitly names box-drawing characters and row-of-boxes-with-arrows. The shipped renderer is a tree-of-IDs. Per the M125 spec, the right fix is the renderer to align with the M103 AC-08 'swimlane' wording.

findings.description: Zero tests for path_graph::render (the new graph renderer module). crates/raul/src/path_graph.rs has no unit tests; the AC-04 verification command 'cargo test -p raul --lib path_graph' returns 0 passed because the module exposes no test surface. The only path-rendering tests cover the comfy-table fallback (commands/path.rs::format_path_lanes) and the wire-level integration (tests/path_cli.rs); neither exercises the actual graph rendering.
findings.author: code-review-agent
findings.rationale: The graph renderer is the primary user-facing artifact of M125 (AC-04 says 'graph is the default'). Without tests, any future refactor can silently regress the output. Per L49 the formatter should be a pure function testable via frozen JSON fixtures, but the current render_graph+render_dag_lane+render_simple_lane are private and untested.

findings.description: Code duplication between crates/raul/src/path_graph.rs and crates/raul/src/commands/path.rs: format_item_label is defined twice (path_graph.rs:190, commands/path.rs:201) and render_simple_lane duplicates the table-rendering loop from format_path_lanes. The graph renderer should call format_path_lanes for the table fallback instead of carrying its own copy of the rendering logic.
findings.author: code-review-agent
findings.rationale: L49 (code-review-lessons.md): extract the formatter as a pure function so unit tests do not depend on dev-binary coupling. The same L49 rule applies to DEDUPLICATION: there should be one table formatter, not two. The duplication is a maintenance hazard (any change to M-prefix logic or empty-lane indicator has to be applied in two places).

findings.description: Dead parameter _name: &str in render_dag_lane (crates/raul/src/path_graph.rs:75). The caller passes name but the function body ignores it. The DAG-tree branch is gated by 'name == "blocked" || name == "execution"' at the call site (line 52), not inside the function. The parameter should be removed.
findings.author: code-review-agent
findings.rationale: Dead parameters are a code smell; the lint machinery already has 1 warning in crates/mp/src/commands/status.rs:12 (unused imports). The dead param is not lint-detectable because the type is &str (unused-function-args rule is off by default), but it misleads readers about the function's contract.

findings.description: M125 scope promised: 'Documentation: update docs/concepts/02 - Getting Started/INSTALL.md ... Cross-link from M102/M103 specs to this milestone as the swimlane half-shipped follow-up.' Neither update was made: (a) path_graph.rs has no module-level docstring explaining what the renderer does or when it falls back to the table; (b) M102/M103 spec files do not cross-link to M125.
findings.author: code-review-agent
findings.rationale: Spec-compliance documentation debt. The cross-link would have surfaced the M103 AC-08 swimlane-vs-table ambiguity to readers of M102/M103. The module docstring would have prevented the spec drift in F-01 by making the rendering contract explicit.

findings.description: Graph mode applies the DAG-tree rendering only to 'blocked' and 'execution' lanes; review/grooming/backlog fall through to render_simple_lane (a comfy-table). M125 AC-04 says 'raul path renders as a swimlane graph ... Each lane is a row' — implying ALL lanes get the graph render, not just two. Currently in graph mode, three of the five lanes look identical to the --table output.
findings.author: code-review-agent
findings.rationale: If the intent is 'graph only for lanes with dep edges', that needs to be explicit in the spec and reflected in the design decision. Otherwise the user expectation mismatch (graph-mode looks like table-mode for review/grooming/backlog) is a UX surprise.

findings.description: AC-01 and AC-04 verifications are recorded as force-bypassed: '[verification force-bypassed: 2 runnable AC(s) failed]'. The verification commands are 'cargo test -p mp --test suite_misc path_lanes && cargo test -p raul --lib path' (AC-01) and 'cargo test -p raul --lib path_graph && cargo test -p raul --test path_cli' (AC-04). Per the workflow, --force is debt and must be resolved; AC-04 still cannot pass cleanly because path_graph has zero tests.
findings.author: code-review-agent
findings.rationale: Force-bypass is documented debt. The AC verification should be re-runnable end-to-end without force.
